title: Affine function-field presentation of the Bertini incidence scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a scheme of finite type over $k$ which is geometrically irreducible over $k$, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module, $V$ a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space and $\psi:V\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$ a $k$-linear map. Assume (i) there are $v_1,v_2,v_3\in V$ and an irreducible component $W$ of $H_{v_2}\cap H_{v_3}$ with $W\not\subseteq H_{v_1}$ and $\operatorname{codim}(W,Y)=2$; (ii) every irreducible component $B$ of $\bigcap_{v\in V}H_v$ has $\operatorname{codim}(B,Y)\ge2$. Fix any basis b of V and let q be its universal incidence projection of [def-zl-bertini-universal-family]. There exist a finite type k-domain A, n>=2 and g_1,...,g_n in A such that V(g_1,g_2) has a component W with dim W+2=dim A, Spec Frac A is geometrically irreducible over k, the universal incidence scheme H is irreducible, q is dominant, and the spectrum of its generic residue-field map Spec kappa(genericPoint H) -> Spec kappa(q(genericPoint H)) is isomorphic, as an arrow of schemes, to Spec Omega -> Spec F, where Omega=Frac(Frac(A)[x_1,...,x_n]) and F=k(x_1,...,x_n,sum_i g_i x_i), as in [lem-zl-bertini-field-extension]. The statement asserts an actual arrow isomorphism, not geometric irreducibility of Omega/F. Dimensions, fields and fibres are as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Conventions: schemes and their residue fields [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], finite type and quasi-compact morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module], section zero schemes [def-pc-zero-scheme], geometric irreducibility [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

proof.text: Apply the proved adapted-chart theorem. It constructs the finite type domain A, functions g, the codimension-two component and geometric irreducibility of Spec Frac A, together with a dominant, stalk-surjective polynomial chart j of the original incidence scheme and the actual coordinate-projection equation. The dense image of the irreducible polynomial spectrum also proves irreducibility of the incidence scheme.

Apply the independent-functions theorem to the component dimension identity. Its algebraic independence gives injectivity of the eliminated parameter substitution, hence dominance of the polynomial parameter projection. The chart equation and cancellation of the coefficient-coordinate isomorphism imply dominance of the original incidence projection.

The polynomial residue-arrow theorem identifies the generic residue-field arrow of the eliminated projection with Spec Omega → Spec F. A dominant chart sends the source generic point to the incidence generic point. Surjectivity on stalks makes its residue-field map an isomorphism: the local ring map is surjective, and its induced field map is therefore both injective and surjective. Naturality of residue-field maps and the coefficient-coordinate isomorphism transport the polynomial arrow isomorphism to the original incidence arrow.

theorem exists_bertiniIncidenceChart
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (Y : Scheme.{u}) [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (L : Y.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [FiniteDimensional k V] :
    letI : Module k Γ(L, ⊤) :=
      Module.compHom Γ(L, ⊤) (Scheme.globalSectionsRingHom k (X := Y))
    ∀ ψ : V →ₗ[k] Γ(L, ⊤),
      (∃ (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) (W : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y),
        Maximal (fun Z : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y ↦
          (Z : Set Y) ⊆ (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ v₂)).zeroLocus.support ∩
            (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ v₃)).zeroLocus.support) W ∧
        ¬ (W : Set Y) ⊆ (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ v₁)).zeroLocus.support ∧
        Order.coheight W = 2) →
      (∀ B : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y,
        Maximal (fun Z : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y ↦
          (Z : Set Y) ⊆ ⋂ w : V,
            ((Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ w)).zeroLocus.support : Set Y)) B →
        2 ≤ Order.coheight B) →
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin r) k V),
        let H := (bertiniUniversalIdeal (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) L
          (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin r) ↦ ψ (b i.down))).subscheme
        let q := bertiniUniversalProjection (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) L
          (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin r) ↦ ψ (b i.down))
        ∃ (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (a : Algebra k A),
          letI := a
          ∃ (hft : Algebra.FiniteType k A) (hdom : IsDomain A),
            letI := hft
            letI := hdom
            ∃ (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (g : Fin n → A),
              (∃ W : Set (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus
                  ({g ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_of_lt hn⟩, g ⟨1, hn⟩} : Set A)),
                W ∈ irreducibleComponents (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus
                  ({g ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_of_lt hn⟩, g ⟨1, hn⟩} : Set A)) ∧
                topologicalKrullDim W + 2 = ringKrullDim A) ∧
              GeometricallyIrreducible
                (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (FractionRing A)))) ∧
              ∃ hI : IrreducibleSpace H,
                letI := hI
                IsDominant q ∧ Nonempty (Arrow.mk
                  (Spec.map (q.residueFieldMap (genericPoint H))) ≅
                  Arrow.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
                    (algebraMap
                      (FieldTheory.bertiniBaseField k (FractionRing A) n
                        (fun i ↦ algebraMap A (FractionRing A) (g i)))
                      (FieldTheory.bertiniOmega (FractionRing A) n)))))
